considered: opened(env, true), which put and rm used to refuse any failed Sync: kept for --fresh and mv, which still fail; a write-mode flag on it instead of to_write would mix two refusals in one function. Store::write and delete kept their one call each, now answering whether the write waits. opcore already does the queue, the replay and the warnings; optokens adds only the transient-Sync fallback, the pending flag and the stderr line.

cut: In src/store.rs, match item IDs directly against opcore’s pending records in all and waits, deleting the intermediate ID vector and waiting helper. In src/init.rs, share one probe-result conversion for write and delete that preserves each step’s refusal and fails either step when its write is pending.
answer: Both made: the waiting helper and its id vector are gone (all and waits match opcore's PendingWrite ids in place); init's probe write and delete go through one reached closure that keeps each step's refusal and fails the step whose write waits. 64 -> 59 net lines.
